title: Tool buttons in the mocks announce as just "button" to a screen reader
goal: Every tool in the design study shows its name on hover, but that name disappears for anyone who cannot see the hover. A person using VoiceOver hears "button" for the Select tool, the ruler, the pen and every other tool in the strip, so the tool bar is unusable without sight. Give each tool its name in a way assistive technology can read.
notes: Found while sweeping the Measure shortcut on 2026-08-24. docs/design/mocks/shared/components/tooltip.js upgrade() copies title into data-tip and then calls el.removeAttribute(chr39)titlechr39(), which drops the accessible name; nothing sets aria-label in its place. Confirmed with a Chrome a11y-tree snapshot of pages/icon-gradient-wt.html: the ten tool-strip buttons all come back as bare "button" with no name. Fix is probably to set aria-label to the label half of the data-tip during upgrade (and in any place that authors data-tip directly, e.g. pages/comp-color.html), then re-snapshot a couple of pages to confirm names appear. Applies to every .tool and every icon-only .btn in the corpus, not just tool strips.
acceptance: Every tool bar button in the design study reports its tool name to assistive technology
The hover tooltip still shows the same name and the same key hint
The name a screen reader reads matches the name the tooltip shows, word for word

log.note: Adversarial review, before building: the mock's own answer (add aria-label everywhere) is wrong in one place. A button with visible text must keep that text as its name, or voice control ("click Delete") stops matching what is on screen. So the rule is narrow: name only a control that has NO name. Also decided the keystroke does not belong in the name, since acceptance asks the name to match the tooltip label word for word; it goes to aria-keyshortcuts instead.
Reproduced first, on pages/icon-gradient-wt.html: a Chrome a11y-tree snapshot returned 21 bare "button" nodes, the ten tool-strip buttons among them.

Fixed in shared/components/tooltip.js. upgrade() now names any tipped control that has no aria-label/aria-labelledby and no visible text, and sweeps EVERY [data-tip] rather than only the ones it just converted from title, since ~69 controls author data-tip by hand. Marker data-tip-named distinguishes our label from an author's.

Two bugs found underneath, both fixed here because they make the name wrong rather than missing. (1) A control that retitles itself for state (playBtn.title = playing ? 'Pause' : 'Play', agent.js dock/float, dock.js collapse/show, img-masking before/after) was skipped by the old [title]:not([data-tip]) selector, so it kept the stale tip AND grew a second native browser bubble with the new text. upgrade() now takes every [title]; a fresh title wins and discards the name derived from the old one. (2) The MutationObserver's 50ms trailing debounce starved outright on a playing timeline: measured ~1093 mutations/sec on video-captions.html, so the sweep after 'play' never ran at all. Added MAX_WAIT 200ms.

shared/components/shell.js: the harvest that turns toolbar chips into .tool buttons kept the original tag, so a <span class="chip" data-target> became a tool-strip button that was not focusable and absent from the a11y tree entirely. Non-native harvested controls now get role=button, tabindex=0 and Enter/Space. Six of these across the lang-* pages.
Named 19 icon-only specimen buttons by hand across comp-buttons, comp-color, comp-index, comp-toolbars, comp-agent, panes-panels.

New gate: shared/check-a11y-names.mjs, in the idiom of check-shortcuts.mjs. Mutation-tested (strip one title -> exit 1). Exempts controls a shared component names at load, each with its reason inline.

Verified on the real corpus, not by inspection: an iframe sweep of all 88 mock pages reports 0 nameless interactive controls (was 23 plus every tool strip), 942/942 .tool named, 2692 controls named from their tip, 0 leftover title attributes, 0 JS errors. The only 4 name/tip differences are hand-written author labels (data-tip-named absent). Tooltip unchanged: #tMeasure still renders 'Measure' + keycap 'I' on hover and on keyboard focus. Cost of the added sweep measured at 0.01ms on the busiest page. All five mock checkers green; Scripts/test.sh 1094 tests pass.
Rule written into shared/AGENTS.md next to the tooltip contract. Audit at queue/audits/2026-08-24-a11y-names.json.

Staging note: this task's epic design-system is staged next, not now. It was small, self-contained and finishable in one pass, so it was completed rather than dropped, but the queue should not hold more design-system tasks while measure-redline is the focus.

Every icon-only control in the design study now reports its tooltip's name to assistive technology, with its keystroke in aria-keyshortcuts. tooltip.js names any tipped control that has no aria-label and no visible text; shell.js gives harvested non-button chips a role, a tab stop and Enter/Space; 19 specimen buttons named by hand. Verified by an iframe sweep of all 88 mock pages: 0 nameless interactive controls (was 23 plus every tool strip), 942/942 tools named, 2692 named from their tip, 0 leftover title attributes, 0 JS errors, and the only 4 name/tip differences are hand-written author labels. Tooltip unchanged (Measure + keycap I on hover and on focus).
